question: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights and/or siren, what should you do?
options: a:Make every reasonable effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, such as pulling to the side and stopping.,b:Speed up to get out of its way without pulling over.,c:Stop in the travel lane and block passage.,d:Continue as normal because they will find another route.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the side and stopping if necessary to provide a clear path for them to pass.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Driving too fast for the conditions,b:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way
note: Traveling at speeds too high for the conditions reduces reaction time and increases crash likelihood; always adjust speed to conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you stop your vehicle?
options: a:At stop signs, red lights, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,b:Only if another car is waiting at the intersection.,c:Only during rush hour.,d:If a pedestrian is nearby even without a crosswalk.
note: You are required to stop at intersections with stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on a multilane road, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes when safe.,b:Always stay at your current speed regardless of traffic.,c:Honk to warn merging drivers.,d:Stop immediately to let them in.
note: On multilane roads, move over when safe to allow entering traffic to merge smoothly and avoid creating a bottleneck.

question: How does alcohol affect driving performance?
options: a:It slows reflexes and reaction time.,b:It improves focus and alertness.,c:It wakes you up and sharpens judgment.,d:It has no effect if you feel sober.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and impairs the skills needed for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a:Yield to vehicles approaching from your right, slow down, cover the brake, and look in all directions,b:Maintain speed and proceed,c:Assume you have the right-of-way and go first
note: At intersections with no signs or signals, yield to the vehicle on your right and be prepared to stop to avoid collisions.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Merging traffic.,c:Pedestrian crossing.
note: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

question: How does increasing your speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It decreases your field of vision making hazards harder to detect.,b:It increases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:It does not affect vision at all.
note: As speed increases, your usable field of vision narrows, so you must be extra alert to hazards.

question: Which steps help you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Increase following distance, avoid driving tired, and keep headlights working.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Drive faster to reduce exposure time.,d:Use high beams all the time.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, avoid driving when tired, and ensure headlights are functional.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left without yielding to oncoming traffic?
options: a:A green arrow pointing left.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A steady red light.
note: A steady green arrow indicates you may proceed in the direction of the arrow with oncoming traffic stopped for the turning movement.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing where there is no traffic light?
options: a:Whoever started moving last.,b:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,c:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle.,d:The driver only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic signals; pedestrians have the right-of-way in these situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure before moving into the passing lane?
options: a:The passing lane is clear and you have signaled your intention.,b:You can pass only on the right.,c:There is no one in the opposite lane.,d:Your passenger opens the door to signal intent.
note: Before passing, confirm the lane is clear and signal to notify other drivers of your lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an unmarked T intersection, who must yield?
options: a:Traffic on the road that ends at the T must yield to through traffic.,b:All vehicles must stop and the first to stop has right-of-way.,c:Drivers on the right always have the right-of-way.,d:The larger vehicle always yields.
note: At an unmarked T, vehicles on the road that ends must yield to traffic on the through road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A Reduced speed 35 mph sign means:
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the sign.,b:The reduced speed starts at the next sign only.,c:You have ample time to slow down after the sign.,d:The change is optional until enforced by a cop.
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates that the new speed limit takes effect at the sign itself.

question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal your intentions in advance, even if no traffic is visible.,b:Signal only when other vehicles are present.,c:Signal only in daylight.,d:Signal only if traveling at high speed.
note: Signaling before lane changes or turns is required by law and is a good safety habit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can fully clear it.,b:Get as close as possible to the car ahead and wait.,c:Enter slowly and inch through the blockage.,d:Use the shoulder to get around the queued vehicles.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking intersections impedes traffic flow and is unsafe.

question: Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving similarly to having what BAC?
options: a:About 0.05 percent, similar to moderate intoxication.,b:0.00 percent — no impairment.,c:0.20 percent — extreme impairment.,d:No BAC equivalent exists.
note: Fatigue impairs driving akin to alcohol; being awake 18 hours roughly equals a BAC of 0.05% impairment.

question: When you meet a car with high, blinding headlights, what is the best action?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.,b:Flash your headlights to warn the other driver.,c:Use your high beams until they dim theirs.,d:Speed up to pass quickly.
note: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on, avert your eyes toward the right side of the road so you are not blinded.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever conditions such as wet roads, poor visibility, or anything else make driving unsafe.,b:Only when you see a police car.,c:Only when entering a busy highway.
note: You must reduce speed below the posted limit when conditions (weather, visibility, road surface) make the posted speed unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center line is a solid yellow next to a broken yellow on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in emergencies.,b:Only if you are on an expressway.,c:You may pass if the broken line is next to your lane and traffic is clear.
note: If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

question: What does a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Yield—slow and give the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians in the intersection,b:Always come to a full stop,c:Slow down only if an emergency vehicle is approaching
note: A triangular red-and-white sign means yield: reduce speed and be prepared to stop to let others proceed first.

question: How can you avoid having to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Honk your horn frequently so others notice you.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance and scan for hazards.,c:Drive in the right lane only.,d:Follow the vehicle ahead very closely to anticipate stops.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead allows you to react smoothly and avoid abrupt emergency stops.

question: If convicted of DUII for the first time, how long will your driving privileges be suspended?
options: a:One year.,b:Six months.,c:Three months.,d:Indefinitely.
note: A first DUII conviction results in a one-year license suspension under Oregon law.

question: What is the correct way to reduce speed when using a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down once you have moved into the exit ramp,b:Begin heavy braking on the main roadway before entering the exit lane,c:Keep your speed constant while on the ramp
note: Do not decelerate sharply on the freeway; move into the exit lane and then brake to slow to ramp speed.

question: When you approach an accident scene, how should you behave if you are not involved?
options: a:Do not stop unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; keep moving and watch for people near the road,b:Always stop to view the scene,c:Park nearby and take photos
note: Do not block emergency responders or create additional hazards; only stop if you are directly involved or help is needed before responders arrive.

question: What does an End school zone sign indicate?
options: a:The reduced school zone speed limit is ending.,b:The school zone speed limit is starting.,c:Children are especially likely to appear here.,d:You must always stop for pedestrians now.
note: An End school zone sign marks the conclusion of the reduced speed school zone and that the special limit no longer applies.

question: At a light rail intersection, what must you always do?
options: a:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all traffic signals.,b:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists only.,c:Ignore the crossing gates if no train is visible.,d:Follow the vehicle directly in front of you across the tracks.
note: At streetcar or light rail crossings always look both ways before turning across tracks and obey all signs and traffic signals; never drive around lowered gates.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly glance over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter,b:Only look at the left side mirror,c:Only check the rearview mirror
note: After checking mirrors, glance over your shoulder to confirm no vehicle is in your blind spot before moving lanes.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safe practice regarding entering a street or crosswalk?
options: a:Do not enter if vehicles are approaching and may not be able to stop.,b:Always insist on right-of-way over vehicles in crosswalks.,c:Enter anytime; drivers must always stop.,d:Run across quickly regardless of traffic.
note: Pedestrians should not step into a roadway when approaching vehicles may not have time to stop, even if the crosswalk legally gives pedestrians the right-of-way.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed choice?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limit,b:Drive faster than the flow to get through quickly,c:Drive slower than the flow at all times
note: Crashes often happen when drivers go much faster or slower than surrounding traffic. Travel with the flow while obeying limits and adjusting for conditions.

question: Which is not a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a direct component.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp, who must yield?
options: a:The driver entering from the ramp should yield to traffic already on the interstate.,b:The drivers on the interstate must always yield.,c:You can force your way in if necessary.,d:Yielding is optional if you are already at highway speed.
note: Vehicles entering from a ramp must yield to traffic on the interstate and merge only when safe to do so.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
options: a:Turn on your headlights (use low beams near other vehicles).,b:Only use parking lights.,c:Not turn on any lights until dark.,d:Use your high beams at all times for better visibility.
note: At dusk or in overcast conditions, turn on headlights and use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Yellow and white.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving the same way.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means which color will soon appear?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing red.,c:Steady green.,d:Flashing yellow.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal is about to change to a steady red.

question: When should you always signal?
options: a:When changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Only when other drivers are nearby.,c:Only if you are turning left.,d:Signals are optional if roads are clear.
note: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, entering/exiting parking spaces, or pulling into traffic to inform others of your intent.

question: After a serious motor vehicle crash, what is your immediate obligation?
options: a:Stop and, if possible, move your vehicle out of traffic; then render aid or call for help,b:Only call the police,c:Continue driving if damage seems minor
note: You must stop at the scene, move to safety if possible, check for injuries, and report the crash to law enforcement when required.

question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving and use the next exit to safely return to your route,b:Quickly cut across lanes to reach the exit,c:Make a U-turn on the highway median
note: Never back up or try to turn around on an interstate; proceed to the next exit and re-route safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do high speeds affect stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Higher speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.,b:High speeds reduce stopping distances.,c:Night driving only affects stopping distance, not speed.,d:Speeds have no effect on crash severity.
note: Driving faster increases stopping distance and the force of impact in a collision, making crashes more severe.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign generally indicate?
options: a:An upcoming hazard or special condition ahead.,b:A nearby school zone.,c:A recreation area ahead.,d:A stop requirement.
note: Diamond-shaped signs typically warn drivers of existing or potential hazards or changes in road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not functioning due to a power outage, how should you proceed?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop, yielding to vehicles in the same manner you would at a four-way stop.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.,c:Park and wait until power is restored.,d:Proceed as if you have the right-of-way.
note: When signals are out, drivers should treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield to vehicles that arrived before them or to the vehicle on the right if arriving simultaneously.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Winter is often the most difficult driving season.,c:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is important during winter.,d:Snow tires can help improve traction on slippery roads.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow, ice, or similar hazardous conditions. Winter driving requires extra caution and proactive vehicle maintenance.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch,b:Turn up the car radio volume,c:Slow down and drive more carefully
note: Take scheduled breaks to rest, walk, and refresh; fatigue greatly increases crash risk on long trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow with a red light, what does it mean?
options: a:You may go straight only.,b:You may proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow, if the intersection is clear.,c:You must wait for a solid green light to move in any direction.,d:You may turn in any direction after yielding.
note: A green arrow with a red light allows traffic to proceed only in the direction of the arrow, provided the intersection is clear.

question: If you must drive in foggy weather, what is the correct lighting choice?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:Drive at the posted maximum speed.
note: In fog, use low beams and reduce speed; high beams or hazards can reduce visibility or confuse other drivers.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When you must stop quickly.,b:When passing another car routinely.,c:To alert others if you have lost control of your vehicle or to warn of imminent danger.,d:To express frustration at another driver.
note: Use your horn to warn others of an immediate danger, such as when you lose control, not to express anger or as a routine signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Stop and look for police vehicles only.,c:Yield to pedestrians and any traffic in the intersection before turning.,d:Always come to a complete stop before turning right on green.
note: When turning right on green you must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles lawfully within the intersection or crosswalk.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers are belted.,b:Be sure only backseat passengers are buckled.,c:Make sure only adult passengers are belted.,d:Start the car then buckle up.
note: Make it a routine to buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or fall back so the other driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace in their blind spot.,c:Stay there; they should check mirrors.,d:Flash your lights continuously.
note: Avoid lingering in another vehicle's blind spot; adjust speed to move out of it so the driver can see you in mirrors.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles and the need to remain visible to their drivers.,b:That trucks can stop instantly.,c:That trucks will always yield to smaller vehicles.,d:That trucks make no noise at night.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances and can block visibility; keep positions where you are visible to truck drivers.

question: Who is most likely to be killed in a work zone crash?
options: a:Drivers and passengers.,b:Bicyclists.,c:Workers and flaggers.,d:Pedestrians on sidewalks.
note: Statistics show drivers and passengers are most likely to be killed in work zone crashes, so drive carefully.

question: If you hear a siren but do not immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull safely to the right curb and stop until you can determine if it is approaching your street,b:Keep driving until you find it,c:Slow down but do not stop until you see it
note: If you hear a nearby siren but cannot locate the vehicle, safely pull over and stop until you confirm it is not headed toward you.

question: Which road users are the hardest to see at night?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.,d:Bicycles with lights on.
note: Pedestrians are hardest to see at night compared to signs or larger vehicles and require extra caution from drivers.

question: If you drink socially, what is a safe choice to ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee to sober up quickly.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.,d:Wait 5 minutes and drive home.
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents driving impaired; coffee or showers do not reduce BAC.

question: What do vehicle brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping,b:That you are making a turn,c:That your emergency brake is engaged
note: Brake lights signal to drivers behind that you are reducing speed or stopping; keep them in working order.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection requires a stop but has no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?
options: a:At the nearest point before entering the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of traffic.,b:Only if you can see 200 feet in both directions.,c:You are not required to stop.,d:In the middle of the intersection to get the best view.
note: Stop at the nearest point before the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic; do not enter the roadway to get a better view.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect driving?
options: a:It is a distracting activity that can take hands and eyes off the road,b:It does not affect driving ability,c:It helps keep drivers alert
note: Handling cigarettes or other smoking tasks diverts attention and movement away from driving, increasing crash risk.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake,b:Only set the parking brake,c:Leave it in neutral and unlocked
note: When leaving a vehicle you must stop the engine, remove the key, lock the ignition, and set the parking brake for safety and legal compliance.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Use alternate routes only.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping distance.,d:Follow the car ahead closely to avoid skids.
note: Slippery conditions increase stopping distances, so increase the space you leave between you and the vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Immediately after passing regardless of space.,c:Only if the other vehicle signals you to do so.,d:At the next intersection.
note: Return to the driving lane as soon as it is safe and there is sufficient space between you and the vehicle you passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you find yourself already within an intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Reverse out of the intersection quickly.,d:Honk to warn others and speed up.
note: If a steady yellow appears while you are in the intersection, continue through carefully rather than stopping abruptly in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, after stopping you should look:
options: a:Right, then left, then right again before proceeding.,b:Left first, then right, then left again.,c:Only at the vehicle ahead and move when it moves.,d:At your rearview mirror for tailgaters.
note: When stopped at an intersection, first glance left, then right, then left again because vehicles from the left are closer.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,b:Never pass them under any circumstances.,c:Flash your lights to make them aware of you.,d:Drive as close behind as possible.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots; avoid lingering beside them and do not tailgate.

question: Drivers may not pass from either direction when the centerline is:
options: a:Double solid yellow.,b:Combination solid and broken yellow.,c:Single broken yellow.
note: A double solid yellow centerline indicates passing is prohibited from both directions.

question: How must drivers treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:They must always be obeyed.,b:They are only suggestions.,c:They apply only when other vehicles are present.,d:They can be ignored at night.
note: Traffic control devices direct traffic and must be followed to ensure safe driving and legal compliance.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing that has more than one track, when should you begin to cross after a train passes?
options: a:Only after you have a clear view down all tracks and are sure no other train is coming.,b:Immediately after the first train clears your lane.,c:As soon as the warning lights stop flashing.,d:When traffic behind you starts moving.
note: At crossings with multiple tracks, wait until you can clearly see all tracks in both directions before proceeding; another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how dangerous is driving at night?
options: a:More dangerous, because visibility is reduced and glare or impaired drivers may be present.,b:Less dangerous due to less traffic.,c:No different in danger level.,d:Safer if you use high beams.
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to decreased visibility, headlight glare, and a higher likelihood of tired or impaired drivers.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what is required?
options: a:Pull to the right curb and stop to allow it to pass.,b:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,c:Continue at the same speed and ignore it.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: You must immediately pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches so it may pass.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,b:Engage four-wheel drive and accelerate more.,c:Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.,d:Drive as close as possible to other vehicles for wind protection.
note: Slowing down and increasing following distance are the most important steps to reduce crash risk on icy or snowy roads.

question: Which strategy best avoids alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive and arrange an alternative ride.,b:Accept drinks but refuse to drive only if you feel drunk.,c:Drink water between alcoholic drinks and drive carefully.,d:Call a friend who will let you drive anyway.
note: The most effective way to prevent alcohol-related crashes is to decide in advance not to drive and arrange a safe alternative before drinking.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark a crosswalk. What must drivers do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and give them the right-of-way.,b:Drive through if no pedestrians are visible.,c:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,d:Only stop for pedestrians if accompanied by a guard.
note: When pedestrians are in a marked crosswalk, vehicles must stop and yield until the crosswalk is clear.

question: Which statement about alcohol and skills is accurate?
options: a:Even small amounts of alcohol can reduce concentration, judgment, and memory.,b:Only BACs above the legal limit cause impairment.,c:Alcohol improves driving at low doses.,d:Alcohol affects only reaction time.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair cognitive and driving skills; no amount is safe for driving.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect your driving?
options: a:It distracts you and makes it harder to stay in your lane and control the vehicle.,b:It makes you a better driver because you are not hungry.,c:It causes no driving errors.
note: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving takes hands and eyes off the road and increases the chance of lane drift and loss of control.

question: What helps a person overcome the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Time only; nothing like coffee or fresh air will sober someone quickly.,b:Drinking tomato juice and lime.,c:Hot coffee.,d:Fresh air and cold water.
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to eliminate alcohol; remedies like coffee or fresh air do not speed sobriety.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII arrest?
options: a:Alcohol, illegal drugs, prescription and over-the-counter medications, and inhalants.,b:Only alcohol beverages.,c:Only illegal drugs, not medicines.,d:Only large amounts of sugar-rich drinks.
note: A variety of intoxicants—including alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some legal medications—can impair driving and lead to arrest.

question: A person carrying a white cane or using a guide dog is most likely:
options: a:Blind or visually impaired and should be yielded to.,b:Participating in a traffic study.,c:Deaf and unable to hear horns.,d:Training for a marathon.
note: Drivers must yield right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

question: When must you stop for a pedestrian?
options: a:When the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,b:Only if they are on your side of the road.,c:Only in clearly marked crosswalks with lights.,d:Only when a crossing guard is present.
note: You must yield and stop for pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the meaning of a green arrow in a traffic signal?
options: a:It is used only on one-way streets.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular green but requires you to move only in the direction shown by the arrow.,c:You may only proceed if accompanied by a circular green light.,d:It is a warning for cyclists only.
note: A green arrow gives the right-of-way to drivers to proceed in the direction indicated by the arrow, provided the intersection is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and safely turn around; do not back up or stop.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,c:Make a U-turn across lanes.,d:Stop immediately and wait for traffic to clear.
note: Do not back up or stop on a freeway; proceed to the next exit where you can safely re-route.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing lanes is which type of line?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Solid yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your car be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:As close to the right side of the street as possible.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.
note: When preparing to make a right turn, move as far to the right as safely possible and do not cut across lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the posted speed and hold up traffic, what is required of you?
options: a:You are always safer than faster drivers.,b:You may refuse to let others pass you at any time.,c:If you are impeding traffic you must pull off the road and let other vehicles pass.,d:You should always stay in the left lane.
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic can be hazardous; if you block traffic you must pull off the road and let others pass.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers only.,b:Human error (driver mistakes),,c:Bad weather alone.,d:Vehicle defects only.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error—mistakes in observation, judgment, or maneuvering while driving.

question: What action best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind the vehicle to check for children and obstacles before getting in.,b:Check rearview mirrors only after getting in.,c:Honk immediately before reversing.,d:Back quickly and rely on mirrors.
note: Because backing limits visibility, always check behind the vehicle before entering it and before you back up.

question: At a railroad crossing where you do not see or hear a train, you must stop when:
options: a:A stop sign is posted, a gate is lowered, flashing lights are active, or a flagger tells you to stop.,b:A train might come in an hour.,c:Only if your passenger says to stop.,d:If the crossing is on a hill.
note: Stop at crossings when required by signs, gates, flashing lights, or flagger instructions, or when a train is visible or too close.

question: Which of these does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce night visibility,c:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle
note: While a flashlight can be useful, it does not directly improve driving visibility at night; keeping glass clean and avoiding heavy tinting do.

question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with an airbag.,b:Airbags can be dangerous to infants or small children even in low-speed collisions.,c:Always make sure every passenger is using a seat belt or appropriate child restraint.,d:Seat belts are optional for adults on short trips.
note: Always fasten your seat belt and ensure children are properly restrained; infants and small children should ride in the rear seat, and never place a rear-facing infant restraint in front of an active airbag.

question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Watch for children walking along the road and proceed with extreme caution.,b:Wait until each child waves to you.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.,d:Honk to alert children to get out of the way.
note: After a bus stops and extends its stop arm, watch carefully for children near the roadway and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainfall?
options: a:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,c:The day after it rains.,d:Only when temperatures are below freezing.
note: Oil on the road surface rises when rain starts, making pavement unusually slippery in the first minutes of a storm.

question: What is the key rule about speed management when approaching curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve to maintain control.,b:Keep posted speed on entry and slow at the sharpest point.,c:Accelerate gently before the curve.,d:Brake hard in the curve for best traction.
note: Because of inertia, reduce speed before you enter a curve so your vehicle stays under control through the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Demand the other driver back up.,d:Pass on the shoulder immediately.
note: On narrow roads, each vehicle should allow at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road so both can pass safely.

question: When riding in a vehicle, how should small children be secured?
options: a:A strong adult can hold a child safely during a trip.,b:Children may stand on the back floor if supervised.,c:Children must be properly secured in an appropriate child seat or seat belt for their size and age.,d:Children should ride without restraints on short trips only.
note: Children must be properly restrained in approved child safety seats or seat belts appropriate for their age and size; never hold a child in your arms as a substitute for a restraint.

question: If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes (ABS) and starts to lose traction, what should you do with the brake pedal?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly while steering to safety.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.,d:Release the brake and downshift immediately.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will pump the brakes automatically to help you stop while you steer out of danger.

question: What does a solid white line between lanes on a multi-lane road mean?
options: a:It separates lanes moving in the same direction and passing is not allowed,b:It separates lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed,c:It separates lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe
note: White lines divide lanes moving in the same direction; a solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes.

question: When must you dim your high beams for an oncoming vehicle to avoid blinding the other driver?
options: a:When the oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet.,b:When the oncoming vehicle is within 400 feet.,c:When the oncoming vehicle is within 450 feet.
note: Switch to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet to avoid blinding the other driver.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using sirens or flashing lights, drivers must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way and pull over to allow it to pass.,b:Ignore it unless it is directly behind you.,c:Speed up to avoid delay.,d:Follow directly behind the emergency vehicle closely to clear the way.
note: Yield to police, fire, or ambulance vehicles using sirens or flashing lights by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until they have passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing unlawful and unsafe?
options: a:Only on hills and curves.,b:Only at intersections.,c:Only at railroad crossings.,d:On hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.
note: It is unsafe and often illegal to pass on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings because visibility and space are limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous as well as speeding.,b:Speeding is never dangerous if you are an experienced driver.,c:You can drive at any speed if no one is around.,d:Higher speed always reduces crash severity.
note: Both excessive speed and driving much slower than traffic can create hazards; speed increases the risk of fatal crashes.

question: If your right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct action to take?
options: a:Pull sharply back onto the road and accelerate.,b:Stop immediately where you are.,c:Take your foot off the accelerator, hold the wheel steady, slow, and ease back onto the pavement when safe.,d:Turn the steering wheel hard left to regain the road quickly.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, remove your foot from the accelerator, steer straight, slow gradually, check traffic, and ease back onto the road when it is safe.

question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?
options: a:Move over to the right if there is an open lane; if not, wait until the road ahead is clear and reduce your speed slowly to encourage them to pass.,b:Brake abruptly to warn them.,c:Increase your speed to create distance.,d:Ignore them and continue your current speed.
note: If you are being tailgated, move right if possible. If you cannot change lanes, gradually reduce speed when safe to encourage the tailgater to go around; never brake abruptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into a crowded freeway, what steps should you take?
options: a:Use mirrors and blind-spot checks, accelerate on the ramp to match freeway speed, and yield to traffic.,b:Enter slowly and expect traffic to stop for you.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp then pull out when clear.,d:Drive on the shoulder briefly to find a gap.
note: Adjust speed on the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield as needed when merging.

question: What are common causes of distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, smoking, talking or texting, and changing audio settings.,b:Driving with both hands on the wheel.,c:Looking at the road ahead.,d:Using turn signals.
note: Distractions include any non-driving tasks like eating, texting, or changing the radio, which reduce attention to driving.

question: When driving in rain, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rainy conditions use low beams to improve visibility and reduce glare; high beams can reflect and reduce visibility.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your left shoulder.,b:Over your right shoulder.,c:Only at your side mirror.,d:At the center console.
note: Glance over the shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to check blind spots.

question: What is the ''No zone'' around a large truck or bus?
options: a:The vehicle's blind spots where the truck driver cannot see other vehicles,b:A special reduced-speed zone,c:A place where stereo use is restricted
note: Large trucks and buses have blind areas on all sides where smaller vehicles disappear from the driver's view; avoid lingering in these zones.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, where should you glance?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road,b:At the vehicle's wheels,c:Toward the left side of the road
note: Look slightly to the right edge of your lane to avoid being blinded while maintaining enough view of the roadway.

question: On a one-way street when an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches you, what must you do?
options: a:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,b:Drive with your flashers turned on.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches on a one-way street, you must drive to the nearest roadside and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey instructions are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs give instructions that must be obeyed; failure to comply can result in penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection but oncoming traffic is heavy, what may you do if the light is green?
options: a:Use the next intersection to turn.,b:Wait behind the crosswalk until traffic clears.,c:Enter the intersection and wait in the center to complete your left turn when it is safe (only if the light is green and the way is clear).,d:Turn on red if it seems safe.
note: If the light is green, you may enter the intersection to wait for a safe gap in oncoming traffic to complete your left turn, provided it does not block traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers when entering the roadway?
options: a:When entering from a garage, alley, or driveway — yield to traffic and pedestrians.,b:Only when your traffic signal is a green arrow.,c:When they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection and you arrived first.
note: Yield to drivers and pedestrians when entering a street from a driveway, garage, or alley; stop before the sidewalk and proceed when clear.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?
options: a:Signal, carefully move off the roadway, and use four-way flashers to warn other drivers.,b:Sit in the car and wait without signaling.,c:Sound your horn repeatedly at passing motorists.,d:Leave the vehicle in traffic and walk away.
note: Turn on hazard flashers, get as far off the road as possible, and display the hood or warning devices so others can see you.

question: If another driver is passing you, what should you do to help them pass safely?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Signal to them when it is safe to pass.,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to let them re-enter safely.,d:Speed up to prevent them from passing.
note: When someone is passing, check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed slightly to allow the passing vehicle to move back into your lane safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you go through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop before entering and ensuring it is safe.,b:After slowing down and checking for cross traffic.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you are stopped in the intersection waiting to make a left turn, how should your wheels be positioned?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight while signaling; do not have wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep wheels turned to the left.,c:Flash your headlights to alert drivers behind you.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision won't push you into oncoming traffic.

question: What do regulatory traffic signs tell drivers?
options: a:What a driver must or must not do,b:About conditions near the road,c:Directions to nearby towns
note: Regulatory signs (often white with black or red markings) indicate laws or rules like speed limits, turn restrictions, and stop/yield requirements.

question: Pentagonal traffic signs are used to indicate:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones and school crossings.,c:Speed limits.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: A five-sided (pentagonal) sign indicates a school zone or school crossing; be alert for children and pedestrians.

question: You need to back out of your driveway and children are nearby. What should you do first?
options: a:Get out and walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn to warn the children.,c:Rev the engine to get their attention.,d:Check the side mirror only and proceed.
note: Before backing into or out of a driveway, exit the car and check behind the vehicle—children can be hard to see from the driver's seat.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side and stop,b:Slow down until it passes,c:Drive with your flashers on
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling to the curb or edge of the roadway and stopping until they pass.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do at the scene?
options: a:Stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, do not stand in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,b:Leave immediately if damage is minor.,c:Stand in traffic to warn other drivers.,d:Drive to the nearest gas station before reporting.
note: Stop, move vehicles out of the flow if safe, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of damaged vehicles after an accident.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much room as possible.,b:Honk to alert them and pass quickly.,c:Use the bicycle lane to get around them.,d:Flash your lights to tell them to move over.
note: Reduce speed and provide plenty of lateral clearance when passing bicyclists; do not crowd them.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:As a stop sign — come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,b:As a green light if no traffic is present.,c:As a warning to speed up.,d:As an indication to yield only to pedestrians.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and then proceeding when it is safe, just like a stop sign.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Keep wheels straight.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must wear a safety belt while a vehicle is moving in Oregon?
options: a:Nobody,b:The driver and all passengers,c:Only passengers under age 16
note: Oregon law requires the driver and every passenger to wear a properly fastened safety belt regardless of seating position. Belts are your best protection in a crash.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should a driver behave?
options: a:Watch for children, be prepared to stop, and yield to pedestrians.,b:Always come to a complete stop no matter what.,c:Sound your horn whenever children are nearby.,d:Speed through quickly to clear the area.
note: When you see a school crossing sign, be alert for children and be prepared to stop; always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle (warning of slow-moving vehicles).,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,d:A circular green sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle; vehicles displaying it typically travel at 25 mph or slower.

question: Why should you be especially alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see and may move unpredictably, requiring extra attention to avoid collisions.,b:They follow completely different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way in all situations.,d:They are required to yield to you at all times.
note: Smaller road users can be harder to detect and may move unexpectedly; drivers must be alert to their presence to prevent collisions.

question: Guide signs are what color and what information do they provide?
options: a:Green — directional and mileage information.,b:Yellow — general warnings.,c:Red — regulatory prohibitions.,d:Blue — destination services.
note: Guide or destination signs are green with white letters and provide directions and distances to locations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill grade, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed and it may be unlawful to pass on a hill where visibility is limited.,b:The truck will always stay at posted speed.,c:You can safely pass on the left at any time.,d:The truck driver must pull over to let you pass.
note: Large trucks often slow on inclines; be cautious about passing on hills with limited visibility, which can be illegal and unsafe.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, why allow extra space in front of your vehicle?
options: a:Because the vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic moves again,b:Because intersections are dangerous,c:Because a stop sign is likely ahead
note: At uphill stops the vehicle in front might roll back slightly when starting; leaving extra space reduces the chance of contact.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee to sober up.,b:Exercise to burn off alcohol.,c:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.
note: The only effective way to lower BAC is to allow your body time to process the alcohol; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not reduce BAC.

question: How should drivers treat railroad crossings?
options: a:As potentially dangerous—always look and listen for trains,b:As safe to cross because trains are rare,c:As safe places to park briefly
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous; obey signals, look both ways, and never cross until it is clearly safe.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, move to a safe area, and stop as soon as you can.,b:Turn off the ignition immediately.,c:Brake hard and park in the lane.,d:Ignore it and continue until the next exit.
note: If power steering stops, you will need more effort to steer; slow down, steer carefully to a safe place, and stop to address the problem.

question: Which of these helps reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allow extra travel time,b:Obey speed limits and use turn signals,c:All of the above
note: Giving yourself extra time, following posted speeds, and signaling intentions all help reduce stress and aggressive encounters.

question: Before moving into the left lane from the right on a multilane highway, what checks should you make?
options: a:Check mirrors, look over your left shoulder for the blind spot, and signal before changing lanes.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and change lanes quickly.,d:Honk to warn other drivers before merging.
note: Always check mirrors and the blind spot by looking over your shoulder, and signal each lane change to alert other drivers.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move to open a clear path, and stop if necessary.,b:Ignore it if other lanes are available.,c:Stop instantly in your lane wherever you are.,d:Speed up to clear the left lane.
note: Provide a clear path for emergency vehicles by slowing and moving to create space; do not try to outdrive the vehicle.

question: Which color typically indicates areas of public recreation or cultural interest on highway signs?
options: a:Orange.,b:Red.,c:Brown.,d:Green.
note: Brown signs are used to indicate areas of public recreation or historical/cultural interest.

question: What is a risk of drinking alcohol while taking medication?
options: a:It can increase the effects of both substances,b:It will reduce the impact of the drug,c:It cures your illness
note: Alcohol and many medications interact to strengthen impairment and health risks; avoid combining them before driving.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:Only behind your vehicle.,c:On all sides of your vehicle (front, rear, left and right).,d:Only on the sides when parked.
note: Keeping a buffer of space on all sides gives you time to react to hazards and reduces the chance of collisions.

question: What does a flashing red light at an intersection indicate?
options: a:You must stop completely and yield; it is the same as a stop sign.,b:The signal is malfunctioning and can be ignored.,c:You may proceed without stopping if no other vehicles are present.,d:You should slow down and continue without stopping.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding when safe.

question: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road with no bicycle lane, what is the safest approach?
options: a:Slow down, wait until no oncoming traffic, and leave sufficient space (at least 3 feet) when passing.,b:Expect the bicyclist to move over and maintain your speed.,c:Pass only at traffic signals or stop signs.,d:Sound your horn and pass closely.
note: Pass bicyclists like other vehicles but allow adequate clearance—at least 3 feet—or more at higher speeds or for groups of cyclists.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:It is okay for drivers to follow motorcycles closely.,b:A motorcycle with two people is more stable than with one.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle to give it full lane width.,d:Motorcycles do not need a full lane.
note: When passing a motorcycle you must move completely into the adjacent lane so the motorcycle has the entire lane width; do not share a lane with it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane is clear.,b:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before making the turn.,c:Enter the intersection and wait for a wave from oncoming traffic.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed slowly.
note: Do not begin a left turn until all lanes you must cross are clear and you can make the turn safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a proper lane available to pass.,b:Whenever you can, even if you must leave the paved roadway.,c:When the road narrows such as on a bridge.,d:Only when the other driver signals you to pass.
note: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is waiting or signaling to turn left and a proper passing lane exists, or when you are on a multilane roadway with two or more lanes moving the same direction. You must not pass by driving off the pavement or main-traveled portion of the road.

question: Compared with smaller vehicles, larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:Larger blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:No blind spots.,d:Blind spots only in the front.
note: Large vehicles such as trucks and SUVs have larger blind spots around the vehicle that require extra caution when passing or following.

question: If you're angry after an incident at work, what should you do before driving home?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before starting to drive.,b:Play loud music to forget about it.,c:Drive fast to let off steam.,d:Call someone and drive while talking.
note: Drivers who are emotionally upset should cool off before driving to avoid impaired judgment and aggressive driving.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line only,b:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line,c:Passing is permitted from either direction
note: When a broken yellow is adjacent to a solid yellow, only drivers on the broken-line side may pass when it is safe.

question: Traffic lanes moving in opposite directions are separated by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Red.,d:Black.
note: Yellow center lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane (leftmost of the destination lanes).,b:The right lane because it may be clearer.,c:Either lane randomly.,d:The bicycle lane even if marked.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the lane nearest to the lane you came from.

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause what effect on a driver?
options: a:Make you drowsy or cause poisoning while driving.,b:Cause your engine to overheat instantly.,c:Improve fuel economy.,d:Prevent your headlights from working.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow toxic fumes into the vehicle, causing drowsiness or death; repair immediately.

question: An advisory speed sign attached to a curve means you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed below the posted limit in poor weather or road conditions.,b:Ignore it when it is raining.,c:Follow it only on highways.
note: Advisory speeds recommend a safe speed for a curve under ideal conditions; reduce speed further in rain, snow, or ice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following describes correct passing procedures?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes, check mirrors and blind spots, and return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:Signal only if another car is beside you.,c:Use your horn instead of signaling.,d:Merge back immediately after pulling even with the other vehicle.
note: When passing, signal at least 100 feet in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and don't return to your lane until you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.

question: If the driver ahead seems distracted (one hand on wheel, talking), what should you do?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space and be prepared for unpredictable actions.,b:Follow their example since they know the route.,c:Tailgate to encourage attention.,d:Pass immediately on the right regardless of safety.
note: Allow extra following distance for distracted drivers because they are more likely to make mistakes.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:By reducing your ability to concentrate on driving tasks,b:By decreasing your chances of being in an accident,c:By making you fall asleep at the wheel
note: Strong emotions or stress reduce concentration and impair driving decisions; it is safer to delay driving if you are emotionally unstable.

question: What should you do to be safe when crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Look and listen in both directions and proceed only when it is safe,b:Cross quickly if a train appears to be approaching,c:Look only when lights are flashing
note: Before crossing tracks, always look and listen for trains from both directions and obey crossing signals and gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes, whenever you want.,b:No; do not pass over double solid yellow lines (except to turn into a driveway or make a left turn where permitted).,c:Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Two solid yellow lines indicate that neither lane may cross the lines to pass, except when turning left into a driveway or entrance where permitted.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots.,b:They rarely obey traffic laws.,c:They do not use headlights at night.,d:They always travel slower than traffic.
note: Motorcycles are harder to see, may be hidden in blind spots, and their speed/distance may be harder to judge.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Warning—hazards or conditions on or near the road ahead,b:Directions to cities and towns ahead,c:Traffic laws and regulations
note: Diamond-shaped yellow signs warn drivers of potential hazards or changes in road conditions so they can take appropriate action.

question: How does being distracted while driving affect your reactions to hazards?
options: a:It usually slows your reaction time and increases crash risk.,b:It makes you react faster.,c:It has no effect on your driving.,d:It only affects new drivers.
note: Distractions reduce drivers' ability to perceive and respond to hazards, increasing the likelihood of a crash.

question: If you're involved in a crash and your vehicle blocks traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible.,b:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for the police before attempting to move it.,d:Leave it and walk away to safety.
note: After a minor collision, move the vehicle off the travel lanes if it's safe to do so, then exchange information.

question: Which actions should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal, check rearview and outside mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Signal only if other cars are present.,c:Check mirrors only and then quickly move.,d:Change lanes without signaling if it’s safe.
note: Always signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do first?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to any pedestrians or vehicles still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly if the path is blocked.,d:Honk to warn cross traffic.
note: A green light allows you to go, but you must first yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.

question: What can impair a person's ability to drive safely besides alcohol?
options: a:Certain medications, illegal drugs, and lack of sleep.,b:Only alcohol affects driving ability.,c:Eating food while driving.,d:Wearing sunglasses.
note: Driving ability can be reduced by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness from lack of sleep.

question: If you begin feeling tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Stop driving and take a break or rest.,b:Open a window to get fresh air and continue.,c:Drink coffee and keep driving.,d:Turn up the radio and speed up.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol; the proper response is to stop and rest rather than continue driving.

question: Which of the following is true about cellphone use while driving in Oregon?
options: a:Drivers under 18 may not talk or text while driving; drivers 18+ must use hands-free when talking.,b:Drivers 18 and older are prohibited from texting while driving but may handhold for calls.,c:Drivers under 18 may talk but not text while driving.
note: In Oregon, drivers under 18 may not use a phone to talk or text while driving. Drivers 18+ must use hands-free for calls; texting is prohibited for all drivers.

question: What documents must a driver produce when stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check?
options: a:Driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.,b:Only their license.,c:Only insurance card.,d:Only the vehicle title.
note: When stopped, the driver must be able to provide their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance.

question: A downward-facing triangular sign typically means:
options: a:School zone ahead.,b:Yield to other traffic.,c:Construction ahead.,d:No U-turn.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign, telling drivers to slow and yield to other traffic or pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What can happen to a bicyclist who fails to obey traffic laws?
options: a:They may be cited or ticketed like other road users.,b:They are exempt from traffic laws.,c:They will always receive only a warning.,d:They are legally required to ride on the sidewalk instead.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers and can be ticketed for violating traffic laws.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against their signal, what must you do?
options: a:Stop or yield to allow pedestrians to cross safely,b:Speed up and pass in front of them,c:Honk to make them hurry
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even when the light is green; ensure they can cross safely before proceeding.

question: A diamond-shaped sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A road hazard or warning.,b:An interstate route.,c:A school crossing specifically.,d:A speed limit.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs used to indicate hazardous conditions or changes in the roadway ahead.

question: A regulatory sign showing a red circle with a slash through a black symbol means:
options: a:The action shown is prohibited.,b:Drivers should stop completely.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.,d:The area is a construction zone.
note: A red circle with a slash over a black symbol on a regulatory sign indicates the depicted action is forbidden.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis' and how can it be prevented?
options: a:Staring at the road for long periods reduces active scanning; prevent it by frequently scanning and taking breaks.,b:Frequent rest stops cause it.,c:Sleeping too much the night before leads to it.,d:Only occurs when driving at high speeds.
note: Highway hypnosis results from staring straight ahead without scanning; avoid it by actively looking around and taking rest breaks.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:On a hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: Parking is unlawful in marked bicycle lanes or on crosswalks; when parking on the street, keep within 12 inches of the curb.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver on the road?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass; do not engage.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Retaliate by tailgating them.,d:Speed up to keep ahead of them.
note: Remain calm, avoid eye contact and provocative gestures, create distance, and let the aggressive driver pass safely.

question: An inattentive driver is someone who:
options: a:Stares off the roadway or daydreams while driving.,b:Maintains eye contact with a passenger when driving.,c:Only watches the vehicle directly ahead of them.,d:Constantly checks mirrors while driving.
note: Inattentive driving includes looking away from the road or daydreaming, which prevents proper scanning and increases crash risk.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go,b:To keep the front wheels straight,c:In the opposite direction of the skid
note: If the vehicle skids, steer in the direction you want the vehicle to travel. When it straightens, correct the steering back.

question: When driving near a motorcycle you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use a full lane.,b:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.,d:Follow closer than you would other vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane width; do not crowd or share the lane with them.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and safely return to your desired route,b:Make a U-turn through the median,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit
note: If you pass your exit, do not stop, back up, or turn across lanes. Proceed to the next exit and re-route safely.

question: What should you do when road surfaces become slippery due to rain, snow, or sleet?
options: a:Reduce your speed below the posted limit and drive with extra caution.,b:Drive at the posted speed because limits are safe in all conditions.,c:Increase your following distance only if others do so.,d:Use cruise control to maintain traction.
note: When roads are slippery, slow down and increase following distance; in many cases safe speed is below the posted limit.

question: What penalties can you face for providing false information on a DMV application in Oregon?
options: a:Driver license suspension or cancellation for one year and possible misdemeanor charges with fines or imprisonment.,b:A brief driving quiz only.,c:Only a small administrative fee.,d:An immediate lifetime ban from driving.
note: Submitting false information on a license or ID application may result in suspension or cancellation of driving privileges for one year and is a class A misdemeanor, punishable by fines and/or imprisonment.

question: When an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren approaches, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop as soon as it is safe.,b:Slow down but remain in your lane.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers only.,d:Accelerate to get ahead of it.
note: When approached by an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, immediately pull to the right and stop to give it a clear path.

question: At a basic crossbuck railroad crossing with no gates or lights, what should you do?
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is near.,b:Turn down your radio to try to hear a train.,c:Always stop even when no train is visible.,d:Drive faster than the train to beat it across.
note: If there are no gates or flashing lights, look and listen carefully and cross only when it is safe to do so.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly,b:You may not see the road between the cars,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals
note: Following too closely reduces your margin to react and stop safely if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly.

question: What color are regulatory signs typically, and what is required of drivers?
options: a:White with black or red markings; they must be obeyed.,b:Blue; they are only suggestions.,c:Green; they are informational only.,d:Orange; they indicate temporary rules only.
note: Regulatory signs are usually white with black or red markings and convey laws or regulations that must be followed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Stop and wait for a green light,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly
note: A flashing yellow means do not stop if unnecessary but slow down, look, and proceed cautiously when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians or other road users already in the intersection,b:Only to drivers turning right,c:No one—you have the right-of-way
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians and other users who are already in the intersection before completing a left turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway before entering.,b:Blow your horn to warn traffic you are entering.,c:Stop with part of your car in the roadway to alert drivers.,d:Drive out quickly to avoid delaying others.
note: When entering from a private road or driveway, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,b:Follow the vehicle ahead even if the flagger disagrees.,c:Ignore the flagger unless a police officer is present.,d:Continue at the same speed.
note: Flaggers control traffic in work zones; obey their signals to protect workers and other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when facing a red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, stop line, or crosswalk as required.,b:Slow down and proceed if there is no cross traffic.,c:Proceed if the crosswalk is clear.,d:Stop only if a police officer is present.
note: A red light requires stopping before the intersection, stop line, or crosswalk and waiting until it is safe to proceed.

question: If you feel worried, nervous, angry, or very emotional, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.,b:Drive immediately; emotions don't affect ability.,c:Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.,d:Call someone while driving to calm down.
note: Strong emotions can distract you and impair driving. Calm down and regain focus before driving to ensure safety.

question: How can you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over the shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use the outside mirror only.,d:Use your turn signal without looking.
note: Turn your head and glance briefly over your shoulder to check areas not visible in mirrors before every lane change.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way,c:Because you are moving faster than the bicycle
note: Cyclists may swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming vehicles may not expect you to move into their path; give bicycles extra room.

question: A round traffic sign usually warns drivers of:
options: a:A no passing zone.,b:A school zone.,c:An upcoming railroad crossing.,d:An upcoming hospital zone.
note: Round traffic signs are typically used to warn of an upcoming railroad crossing.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Move the injured person away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave injured people where they are and avoid providing aid.,c:Avoid moving the injured unnecessarily, keep them warm, and provide first aid until help arrives.
note: Do not move injured persons unless absolutely necessary; control bleeding, keep them warm, and wait for trained emergency responders.

question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down as you enter the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,b:Increase speed as you enter and then brake sharply at the exit.,c:Maintain a single constant speed throughout the curve.,d:Brake hard throughout the curve to stay slow.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and then increase speed smoothly as you exit to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection of two similar roads, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle that honks first.,d:The fastest vehicle.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, yield to vehicles approaching from your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Cross into the oncoming traffic lane only when it is safe and legal.,b:Use the shoulder to pass when necessary.,c:Flash headlights at oncoming traffic to warn them.,d:Pass on the right anytime.
note: Passing on two-lane roads requires entering the oncoming lane if and only if it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Where is it especially important to reduce speed?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, near intersections or railroad crossings, and when the road is wet or slippery.,b:Only on open highways.,c:Only when directed by a policeman.,d:Only when driving behind a slow-moving vehicle.
note: Reduce speed in narrow or winding areas, at intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills and blind curves, and whenever road conditions are poor.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Possibly run into the street without looking, so slow down and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Know when it is safe to cross.,d:Yield to your vehicle.
note: Children may act unpredictably and could run into the road without looking; reduce speed and be prepared to stop.

question: How would you best describe distracted driving?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior that endangers you and others.,c:Something of little concern.,d:A behavior only new drivers engage in.
